Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus-withdrawal chromatin accessibility time course (ATAC-seq + CUT&Tag)
ideas.description: Stimulate cells transiently (e.g., TNF, wounding, or inflammatory signal), then remove the stimulus and track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and ATAC accessibility at its target enhancers over days to weeks. Persistent accessibility or H3K27ac at AP-1 motifs after AP-1 binding itself has decayed ('trabea' like a lingering vesting, a residual mark) would indicate AP-1-established memory, as in the epigenetic 'scars' of inflamed epithelium.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion at priming vs. recall stages
ideas.description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on FOS/JUN family members (or dominant-negative A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either during the first stimulus, during the rest interval, or only at re-stimulation. If depleting AP-1 only during priming abolishes the faster or stronger secondary transcriptional response, whereas depletion during rest has no effect, AP-1 is needed to write memory but not to maintain it; the opposite pattern shows it carries memory actively.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage/history barcoding
ideas.description: Perform paired scRNA/scATAC-seq on cells with and without prior stimulation, with a heritable barcode or fluorescent AP-1 reporter recording previous exposure. Test whether AP-1 motif accessibility (chromVAR) and memory-gene expression stay correlated across cell divisions in clonal lineages, separating heritable (mitotically stable) memory from transient signaling noise.

ideas.title: Live-cell AP-1 reporter and optogenetic pulse patterning
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN or an AP-1 transcriptional reporter while delivering controlled optogenetic or ERK-pulse inputs of varying duration, frequency, and rest interval. Fit input-history-dependent response curves (hysteresis, paired-pulse enhancement) to determine whether the system integrates past dynamics and for how long, giving quantitative memory timescales.

ideas.title: Targeted perturbation of memory-associated AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Use CRISPRi/dCas9 epigenome editing or motif mutation at selected AP-1-bound enhancers (identified by persistent accessibility) after priming, and combine with Hi-C/Micro-C to look for retained loops. Test whether disrupting the AP-1 site or its recruited BAF/SWI-SNF chromatin remodeling erases faster re-induction of linked genes, establishing sufficiency and necessity at specific loci rather than genome-wide correlation.
